name: code_search
description: Search Ledgerline's private codebase (every text file except config/) for a literal, case-insensitive substring of one line. It matches the text of lines, never file names. Use it to find which files contain an identifier, an error message or a word from the issue, then read the likeliest file with code_read_file. Returns JSON {query, query_valid, path_glob, source, count, shown, truncated, index_age, results}, each result {path, line, text}, in path order. count is the total number of matching lines; at most max_results of them (a cap of 20) are shown, and truncated is true when more matched than were shown: then by_file lists, as {path, count}, the at most 10 files with the most matches; narrow the query or add a path_glob. Zero matches is a success, not an error: count 0, query_valid true, results empty. It means the text appears on no line: try a shorter identifier or another word, not the same query again. A malformed query (empty, longer than 200 characters, or a path_glob that is not a valid glob) is an error that says what to change. index_age says how old the index is: with source index, a file changed since then can be missing or stale.

query.description: The literal text to find, 1 to 200 characters, matched case-insensitively within single lines. Shorter finds more: one identifier (backoffDelay) or one exact phrase of an error message works best. Several words match only where they appear together, in that order, on one line. Not a regular expression: no wildcards, operators or quotes.

path_glob.description: null searches every file, the usual choice. A glob relative to the repository root, such as src/api/** or **/*.tsx, searches only the paths it matches: fewer, less noisy results when you already know the area. Only letters, digits, / . _ - and the wildcards * ? [ ] { }; no leading /, no .., no spaces.

max_results.description: How many matching lines to show, 1 to 20; 10 is the usual choice. Each shown hit costs about 30 tokens in concise format. count reports every match whatever this is, so a small value still tells you how many there were.

response_format.description: concise, the cheap default: each hit's path, line number and at most 120 characters of the line. detailed: at most 240 characters of the line plus the line before and after it, about three times the tokens; choose it only when the surrounding lines decide which file to read.

source.description: index, the default: the prebuilt index, fast; index_age says when it was built. live: reads every file from disk, slower and always current; choose it when index_age is old and the issue mentions a recent change, or when an index search found nothing for text you are sure is there.

examples.note: Typical: one identifier, every file, ten hits, concise, from the index.

Hard: a two-word phrase matches only lines that contain it exactly; the glob limits the search to TypeScript under src/, and live reads the files themselves. If this returns count 0, that is an answer: search for one word instead.
